problem: Staged translation of committed Hayai OCR blocks took the legacy full-page detection/OCR prompt. The model merged/reordered text and regenerated numeric IDs; the keep-block application bound those IDs to old balloons, then retained old source text while copying mismatched translations.
fixes: Route nonempty committed Hayai keep-mode sources through the existing immutable fixed-block protocol. Preserve each input source, candidate ID, geometry and slot; do not regroup adjacent fragments or ask the model to re-OCR them.
Retain reviewStatus through keep-block overlay application and staged workflow merge so repaired/fallback results remain reviewable.
Clarify Japanese-to-Korean colloquial/mimetic translation and incomplete-clause handling. This improves some samples but does not eliminate semantic model errors.

method.scope: 24 other works, two pages each, plus one non-explicit introduction page from the reported work; 49 page workflows per model per variant. The reported chapter was audited across all 44 saved page request/response records; only its introduction page was re-inferred.
method.isolation: Original image copies and separate Electron userData/library/log/settings roots; shared existing native/model caches. Production Hayai OCR generated once and frozen for before/after comparisons. The reported page restores ten input blocks from the original saved request in the isolated copy.
method.settings: Japanese to Korean, Hayai GPU OCR, Gemma local CUDA12 profile, Q4_K_M, empty work context, cumulative context off, font matching off. Detection/OCR/translation only; no erase, typesetting or export stages.
method.hardware: Windows, NVIDIA RTX 4090 24 GB, driver 610.88; llama.cpp mainline b11146 CUDA 12.4 runtime. AMD/macOS/RTX 20 hardware was not exercised in this translation audit.

metricMeaning: Source changes and exact cross-assignment compare parsed output jp to normalized input jp at the same ID. Fixed protocol reconstructs jp from immutable inputs, so zero source changes is a structural invariant, not proof that every Korean sentence is semantically correct. The separate visual review checked the actual ko against source balloons.

downstreamExclusions.explanation: Existing downstream filtering removes seven punctuation-only blocks and one page-number block. All 283 requested slots were returned by the fixed model protocol. These eight exclusions also occur with baseline 12B and were not introduced or changed by this patch.

limits: This is a targeted regression investigation and a 24-work sample, not an exhaustive read of every manga in the download directory.

12B still exhibits semantic mistranslations in short expressions, particles, apologies and kinship terms. 26B still has some awkward fragments and context-dependent terminology. Correct block ownership is not a guarantee of perfect translation.
Existing OCR misrecognition is preserved by committed-source translation. Re-reading/correcting OCR remains a separate operation. The model can still infer context in ko despite instructions.
Existing saved chapter translations were not overwritten. Restart the development app and rerun translation to apply the fix; fix visibly wrong OCR first where needed.
PaddleOCR, global development tools, model assets and native CUDA/AMD/Metal runtimes were not modified.

baselineFocused.note: Baseline used four focused files; expanded final focused suite used eleven files. Counts are not a same-scope test-growth metric.

reproduction: Use corpus-selection.json for image inventory and SHA-256; inputs/*.ocr.json contains the frozen production OCR.

Build Electron and run scripts/prepare-runtime.cjs, then launch app-audit.cjs with Electron, arguments: translate 12 <unique-tag>, then translate 26 <unique-tag>. Do not overwrite baseline/fixed/final runs.
Run analyze.cjs and visual-review.py; inspect every comparison image. The local harness and original manga are intentionally excluded from Git.
rollback: Revert the translation-alignment fix commit and restart the app. No user-library migration or native runtime rollback is needed.
